subject: Jurisdictional contingency play + on‑prem peering Q&A

Subject: Private deploy: EU/APAC contingency questions before SOW

Diego — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Before we move to SOW sign, Legal and Infra asked for a short written note on two items we didn't close out:

1) Control plane placement: we need to understand options where control-plane APIs (token issuance, admin APIs) remain within our EU VPC boundary except for telemetry. Can Redwood support a split control-plane (customer-hosted admin plane + Redwood service for orchestration) and what are the implications for latency and failover?

2) Cross-border fallback: if APAC site loses outbound peering to our provider (simulated outage), we need a deterministic plan that prevents user data egress to non-EU/APAC jurisdictions. Can you sketch the runtime routing and how the warm-standby in EU would take over without touching US-hosted endpoints?

We attached our security Qs (ACME_Security_QA_Responses.pdf) and would prefer answers in plain bullets. Also copying Tom at EdgeOps — they'll be doing the MPLS/direct‑peering with our colo.

Thanks,
Sana
Sana Patel
Sr. Infrastructure Lead, ACME Corporation

Subject: Re: Private deploy: EU/APAC contingency questions before SOW

Sana — appreciate the clear asks. High level answers first, followed by an appendix with failure-mode specifics we can include in the SOW: 

- Control plane split: Yes — Redwood supports a hybrid control-plane model for Private deployments. There are two supported patterns:
  * Customer-managed admin plane (preferred for strict residency): customer runs a lightweight control API in their VPC that handles token minting and admin actions; Redwood’s hosted orchestration communicates over a mutually authenticated mTLS channel limited to orchestration tasks only.
  * Segregated hosted control plane with per-customer tenancy: Redwood-hosted control plane, but all sensitive admin calls are proxied through an EU resident gateway you manage.

  Operational implications: latency for admin ops will depend on the colo/VPC connectivity. Token issuance in the customer-hosted model is sub-100ms on direct peering; in the proxied model expect 150–300ms depending on SASE/MPLS. Both options support offline key caching for short-lived tokens so runtime inference is local to the serving cluster.

- Cross-border fallback / deterministic failover: we recommend a deterministic failover flow that avoids US egress:
  1) Traffic failover is driven by your routing policy at the edge (BGP community: REDWOOD-AUTO-FALLBACK).
  2) When APAC loses upstream reachability, edge marks routes with a no-egress community and announces to Redwood’s peering fabric.
  3) Redwood runtime will divert affected sessions to EU warm‑standby clusters that are pre-provisioned with KV cache snapshots (we snapshot per-tenant prefixes every 60s to S3 in-scope EU buckets).
  4) Control-plane calls for key operations will continue to be handled by your EU admin plane. If the EU admin plane is unreachable, our fallback is constrained to read-only inference that uses cached authorization (no new data writes).

  That flow prevents any client traffic from transiting US-hosted control endpoints. We will include explicit BGP community mappings and a test drill in the SOW.

Next actions: I’ll add Karthik and Naomi to draft the technical annex (network diagram, BGP communities, KMS handoff) and Marissa will propose SOW language for the legal hold/KMS commitments. Attaching an internal network diagram for the recommended peering layout.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Sana — sending the technical annex highlights (short bullets) below; we can iterate. I'll attach the annex diagram and the MPLS/BGP snippets for your edge team.

1) On-prem peering options we suggest:
   - Direct MPLS/Direct Connect (best for deterministic routing & latency SLAs) — requires XFR route maps, private AS on your colo.
   - IPsec over SASE (works if you want SASE inspection) — adds ~30–80ms depending on region, defines egress controls via SASE policy.
   - Mixed: BGP over MPLS with a secondary SASE tunnel for telemetry/control.

2) BGP failover policy (suggested):
   - APAC announces with community 65000:100 -> normal.
   - On-loss-of-upstream, edge rewrites to 65000:200 (no-egress) and withdraws default-route to upstream provider. Redwood edge fabric watches the community and triggers session drain + rehydrate to EU warm‑standby.

3) KMS / key escrow behaviour:
   - Primary keys reside in your EU KMS/HSM (customer-managed).
   - For warm standby, we support a split‑wrap key model: a short-lived session key encrypted by your HSM and an ephemeral Redwood wrap key. Key unwrapping requires a two‑party approval (customer API + Redwood orchestration token) — documented in annex.

4) Operational playbook & drills:
   - Quarterly cross-border drill with pre-populated traffic and runbooks.
   - Telemetry suppression: logs that include token metadata must be scrubbed before leaving region. We'll provide config templates for fluentd/otel to enforce this.

I'll prepare the annex doc (pdf) and SOW clauses for Legal review next. If ACME infra can share a colocation contact and ASN, we can draft BGP samples.

Karthik
Director, Deployment Engineering, Redwood Inference

Diego/Karthik/Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple legal items we want to call out to include in the SOW language (short list):

- Residency guarantee clause: explicit commitment that customer data (tokens, prompt logs, KV snapshots) will not egress beyond the named jurisdictions during normal operation or during the failover flow you described. Exceptions need pre-approved by ACME Legal with documented mitigation.
- Audit & proof: we need an agreed set of telemetry artifacts (BGP announcements, control-plane call logs, S3 object manifests for the KV snapshots) to be provided within 24 hours after a failover event.
- KMS SLA: we need an escalation path if the customer's HSM becomes unavailable and Redwood cannot unwrap keys — what are timeboxed remediation steps and optional temporary escrow?

If you can draft SOW clauses addressing the three items above, ACME Legal will review and provide comments. We anticipate sign-off pending those items.

Ben Cho
Counsel, ACME Corporation
